PS 01 · Problem statement

The question

A company has received a contract to construct a shopping mall with 7 interconnected blocks and 3 levels of underground parking on an 8-acre site. The total estimated concrete requirement is about 12,000 m³.

Theme

Complete all paperwork related to the local governing body and RERA, and develop a detailed site layout for efficient circulation of labour housing, material storage and the civil site office.
Site width400 ft
Site depth871 ft
Total block area1,18,000 sq ft
GatesSouth & North
Blocks 1 & 3Near Gate 2
Blocks 6 & 7Near Gate 1

The eastern side is an open zone available for the labour camp, material storage and site offices.

Concrete supply — RMC vs own batching plant

RMC is delivered by transit mixers from automated batching plants with retarders for slump retention, then placed by static pumps, booms or tower-crane buckets. Compaction uses 40/60 mm needle vibrators, and curing is by ponding (slabs), wet hessian (columns) and curing compounds (vertical faces).

4
Reflection

What I learned


Paperwork comes first

Before any concrete is poured, ownership, land-use and design approvals have to be in place. Listing every land and design document showed how much groundwork a site needs.

Layout is logistics

Placing gates, blocks, the labour camp and storage yards decides how smoothly men and materials move. Planning the site on drawings made circulation and safety real.

Theory met the site

Talking with Mr. Sufiyan and seeing block stacks, formwork and equipment made our storage and labour figures easier to judge.

Numbers drive decisions

Breaking RMC and own-plant costs into materials, labour and vehicles turned a gut feeling into a clear choice. Teamwork split the job well.

5
Conclusion

Our recommendation


For 12,000 m³ of concrete, the own batching plant (₹5,37,43,236) is more economical than RMC (₹6,84,00,000) — a saving of about ₹1.47 crore (≈21%).

With the statutory documents compiled and a layout that separates the labour camp, sanitation, storage yards and offices on the open eastern side of the 8-acre site, the project is ready to move to the next stage.

Solutions

Our approach


DRAFT · add your site visit and engineer interaction

Site visited & interaction with engineer

The 22 Aug 2026 visit to the Manjunath Nagar / Pavaskar Layout site with site engineer Mr. Sufiyan (see PS1) showed practices relevant to this statement. Add what you observed or asked him.

Four-copy invoice control

Original to accounts, copies to store, site engineer and supplier acknowledgement, so no delivery is paid without a matching store entry.

ACCEPT / HOLD / REJECT

Conforming material is accepted; material awaiting test reports is tagged HOLD and segregated; non-conforming material is rejected and sent back.

Storage codes

Every zone is coded, from CS-01 (cement store) to RJ-01 (reject yard), so stock can be located and audited quickly.

15-day commissioning plan

Set up the gate, weighing, inspection bay, stores and accounts records in the 15 days before the first major deliveries.

Reflection

What I learned

A material system is only as strong as its paperwork. Linking each delivery to an order, an inspection result and a store code showed me how leakage and disputes are prevented before they start.

Conclusion

The outcome

A coded, four-copy, three-decision system gives full traceability from purchase order to consumption and keeps rejected material out of the works.

Site visited & interaction with engineer

The 22 Aug 2026 visit to the Manjunath Nagar / Pavaskar Layout site with site engineer Mr. Sufiyan (see PS1) showed practices relevant to this statement. Add what you observed or asked him.

Traceable datum

Carry a known benchmark to the site and fix site PBMs, with closed levelling loops recorded in a register.

PBMs and TBMs

Protected permanent benchmarks outside the work zone, with temporary benchmarks transferred to each block and floor.

Visit plan

A specialist survey agency for control and major set-outs, with an in-house surveyor for day-to-day levels and alignments.

Independent check

Setting-out is released for work only after a second person has checked it against the drawing.

Reflection

What I learned

Small survey errors multiply across seven blocks and three basements. A single traceable datum with independent checks is cheap compared with the cost of rework.

Conclusion

The outcome

A protected, traceable benchmark system with specialist and in-house surveys and an independent check before release keeps all blocks and levels consistent.

Solutions

Our approach


DRAFT · add your site visit and engineer interaction

Site visited & interaction with engineer

The 22 Aug 2026 visit to the Manjunath Nagar / Pavaskar Layout site with site engineer Mr. Sufiyan (see PS1) showed practices relevant to this statement. Add what you observed or asked him.

BBS discipline

Prepare and approve the bar bending schedule for each element before ordering, so only the required lengths and sizes are bought.

Cutting optimisation

Plan cuts against standard bar lengths and reuse offcuts for short bars and spacers.

Offcut register

Record every offcut and its reuse so wastage can be measured against the estimate.

Tagged storage

Store steel by diameter and grade on raised racks with tags; keep a panel-life record to track how many times each formwork panel is reused.

Reflection

What I learned

Wastage looks like a site problem but is largely a planning problem. Tying purchase to BBS and cutting plans shows where money is saved.

Conclusion

The outcome

BBS discipline, cutting optimisation, registers and tagged storage reduce steel and formwork wastage before it happens and make the remainder measurable.

Quantity × productivity

Review and roll the plan forward every two to four weeks using actual progress.

Welfare, safety, output

Housing, sanitation, induction and PPE are part of the plan, and measured output per crew is recorded.

Reflection

What I learned

This links directly to my PS1 work on labour housing: a camp for 280 workers only makes sense if the stage-wise plan says when those workers are needed.

Conclusion

The outcome

A rolling, productivity-based labour plan keeps crews matched to each stage and keeps welfare and safety measured, not assumed.

Solutions

Our approach


DRAFT · add your site visit and engineer interaction

Site visited & interaction with engineer

The 22 Aug 2026 visit to the Manjunath Nagar / Pavaskar Layout site with site engineer Mr. Sufiyan (see PS1) showed practices relevant to this statement. Add what you observed or asked him.

Immediate response

Check the records above, hold the related pour records and keep spare cubes.

Find the cause

Review sampling, curing, testing machine, batch records, water and materials, and slump at the time of casting.

Competent assessment

If doubt remains, the structural engineer decides on non-destructive tests and core tests before any action on the member.

Responsibility and prevention

Contractor QA, the concrete supplier or batching plant, the testing lab and the engineer-in-charge each answer for their stage; corrective action is recorded and the process fixed.

Reflection

What I learned

A failed cube is a signal, not a verdict. The investigation has to be systematic and fair to each party before it can be fixed.

Conclusion

The outcome

Verify first, find the cause, let a competent engineer assess the structure, then assign responsibility and prevent a repeat.
